change: one byte changed inside the loader's signature area, Secure Boot switched off
wrong_if: The prediction is wrong if the boot is refused or hangs: with Secure Boot switched off the changed loader is expected to run to its last line.
It is wrong if register 4 differs from the normal run. The changed byte lies in the signature area, and the expectation is that the image digest this firmware measures does not cover that area.
It is wrong if the record differs from the pilot e4 (Secure Boot switched off, nothing else changed) in any row below: another first differing event than 4, or any differing register besides 7.
not_scored: This run changes two things against the normal run: the switch and the byte. The pilot e4 changes the switch alone. The rows therefore predict that this run equals e4, which is the same as predicting that the byte adds nothing a recording can see. A comparison is always made against a normal run, so that equality is spelled out row by row.
The changed file has another SHA-256 than the signed loader and the same Authenticode digest. Both follow from how the file was changed, not from the boot, so they are not rows.

byte.what_it_is: Byte 128 of the 256 bytes of the signature value: the number that was made with the signer's private key over the signed attributes. It is not part of the certificate, of the digest that was signed, or of the padding. Its lowest bit is flipped.
